name: mssql-mcp
description: A Model Context Protocol server for Microsoft SQL Server, built in C#/.NET 10, with Restricted and opt-in Unrestricted access modes.
description_good_justification: README.md:1-3 (project name, tagline, and summary of what mssql-mcp does). Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
interact_justification: README.md supported-clients section lists MCP harness wiring for Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline, Continue, opencode, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Hermes, Kiro, Zed. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md:1-3 describes how to contribute, PR process, and standards. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md:143-164 lists PR checklist, Conventional Commits, branch protection, and code-review expectations. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
floss_license_justification: LICENSE is MIT; README.md Trademarks & licensing section links to LICENSE. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is OSI-approved; LICENSE file contains standard MIT text. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
license_location_justification: LICENSE at repository root; README.md and docs/security-posture.md link to it. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
documentation_basics_justification: README.md covers install, configuration, tools, examples, troubleshooting, security, development; docs/adr/README.md indexes 35 ADRs. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
documentation_interface_justification: README.md Tools section and ADR-0016 document the 9 MCP tool schemas and return shapes. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
sites_https_justification: All distribution URLs and badge links in README.md use https://github.com, https://nuget.org, https://npmjs.com, https://bestpractices.dev. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
discussion_justification: README.md Contributing section points to GitHub Issues for bugs/features; SECURITY.md points to private vuln reporting. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
english_justification: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, and all ADRs are written in English. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
maintained_justification: Recent commits include security audits (2026-07-22 and 2026-07-24), scorecard.yml workflow, and active branch protection; README stability section shows 0.x active maintenance. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
repo_public_justification: GitHub repository is public at github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
repo_track_justification: Git commit history records changes, authors and timestamps; public pull requests retain reviewable interim revisions. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/commits/main/
repo_interim_justification: No opaque intermediary; commits go directly to GitHub via PR workflow. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
repo_distributed_justification: Git is a distributed VCS; every clone has full history. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
version_unique_justification: release.yml uses Git tags as source of truth; npm and NuGet versions are synced to the tag via scripts. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
version_semver_justification: Tags use `v*.*.*` (Semantic Versioning); README stability section references 0.x series. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
version_tags_justification: release.yml triggers on `push: tags: 'v*.*.*'` and release-please creates versioned release PRs. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
release_notes_justification: release.yml uses `gh release create --generate-notes` for GitHub Release notes; release-please generates CHANGELOG entries. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: The repository advisory inventory contains no records, but a disclosure SLA is not proof that every publicly identified runtime vulnerability appears in its fixing release notes. Review published release notes against the public audit identifiers before certifying applicability/compliance. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/releases
report_process_justification: README.md Contributing section and SECURITY.md:5-7 describe GitHub Issues for bugs and private vulnerability reporting. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues are enabled; #140 tracks actual external assessment submission, while historical #68 completed repository documentation/badge wiring. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
report_responses_justification: API inventory on 2026-10-02 found 77 owner-authored issues and no non-owner/non-bot reports; there was no external bug-report response sample to measure. A published SLA alone is not evidence of response performance. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
enhancement_responses_justification: The same public inventory contained no external-author enhancement requests; CONTRIBUTING.md documents the request process. Reassess when an actual response sample exists. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues and Security Advisories archive reports; docs/security-audits/ archive point-in-time audits. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md:1-7 documents private GitHub vulnerability reporting and forbids public issues. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md:5-7 explicitly uses GitHub's private vulnerability reporting and says "Do not open a public issue". Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: Repository advisory API returned no records on 2026-10-02, so no report-response interval was available to assess. Verify any privately received reports before submission; the published SLA is not execution evidence. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
build_justification: `dotnet build mssql-mcp.sln` builds all src and test projects; CI runs it on every push/PR. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
build_common_tools_justification: .NET SDK 10, `dotnet restore`, `dotnet build`, `dotnet pack`, `dotnet test` are standard .NET tooling. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
build_floss_tools_justification: Build uses only standard .NET SDK and open-source Node tooling; all build tooling is free/libre. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
test_justification: Observed integrated run: 461 unit cases and 486 full opt-in disposable SQL Server cases passed, zero failures and four existing unreachable-case skips in each. Real MCP sequence rejection and same-session recovery, log-path rejection and CLI invalid-mode startup refusal were separately exercised. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
test_invocation_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md:46-47 documents how to run unit and integration tests. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
test_most_justification: Actual Coverlet.MTP live-SQL measurement before the last configuration-only repair: production Core + Tools 84.5% line / 80.3% branch. Native V8 npm security regressions measured shim branch coverage 85.9%. These are scoped measurements, not whole-repository coverage or proof of all input combinations. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: CI runs build, format, unit, offline npm, native CLI/SQL and live container SQL checks on push/PR. The real MCP stdio Inspector check is separately mandatory before pushes; do not claim it runs in hosted CI. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md:64-79 pre-push checklist mandates passing tests; ADR-0031 documents unknown-argument dispatch and pre-push discipline. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
tests_are_added_justification: Recent Guard sequence-allocation, linked-log-path and invalid-access-mode repairs include public-behavior regressions; the updated unit and disposable SQL suites passed. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/tests/mssql-mcp.Core.Tests/GuardTests.cs and https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/tests/mssql-mcp.Core.Tests/FileLoggerProviderTests.cs
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md:148-149 and PR checklist require tests for new code; tests follow project layout naming. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
warnings_fixed_justification: CI `dotnet build` and `dotnet format` are clean; security audit confirms warnings treated as errors. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
warnings_strict_justification: Warnings are errors and latest-recommended .NET analyzers are enabled, with six explicit, documented suppressions in ADR-0020; strictness is practical, not a claim that every possible rule is enabled. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
know_secure_design_justification: ADRs document threat-aware design, but the criterion requires a primary developer's knowledge, not merely documentation. A primary developer must confirm the detailed secure-design requirements before submission. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
know_common_errors_justification: Security documentation identifies relevant error classes and mitigations; a primary developer must personally confirm the knowledge criterion. An AI review cannot make this attestation. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
crypto_published_justification: The npm shim uses SHA-256 through Node's crypto library and HTTPS through Node's TLS stack; SQL transport encryption is implemented by SqlClient, not a custom protocol. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
crypto_call_justification: `npm/bin/mssql-mcp.js:sha256Hex` calls Node `crypto.createHash('sha256')`; HTTPS uses Node's library, and SQL TLS is delegated to SqlClient. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
crypto_floss_justification: Cryptographic functionality uses FLOSS Node/OpenSSL and Microsoft.Data.SqlClient implementations; no proprietary cryptographic implementation is required. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
crypto_keylength_justification: SHA-256 is used for archive integrity, but negotiated TLS keys depend on the runtime, SQL Server and operator settings. No evidence establishes all default TLS key lengths or that smaller keys can always be disabled. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
crypto_working_justification: The project's explicit integrity hash is SHA-256, not a broken hash. HTTPS and default SqlClient encryption use maintained TLS implementations; operator-selected SQL settings can weaken transport protection. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The SHA-256 call is supported, but no exercised TLS/cipher-policy evidence establishes absence of serious weaknesses across operator-configured SQL connections and platform runtimes. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
crypto_pfs_justification: TLS handshakes and negotiated key agreement were not inspected. Delegating TLS to libraries does not make perfect forward secrecy inapplicable or prove it. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
crypto_password_storage_justification: The project does not store password verifiers for authentication of external users. Operator SQL credentials are a different concern; environment configuration is recommended, and the supported CLI flag does not establish an absence of argv exposure. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
crypto_random_justification: Project code does not generate cryptographic keys or protocol nonces; TLS key/nonce generation is delegated to maintained cryptographic libraries. Temporary-directory names are not a claim about cryptographic nonce generation. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
delivery_mitm_justification: GitHub archive/checksum downloads and npm/NuGet registry delivery use HTTPS. Archive checksums, requested attestations and npm provenance are additional controls whose actual per-release evidence must be checked. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
delivery_unsigned_justification: The npm shim retrieves checksum sidecars over HTTPS, not unsigned HTTP. This criterion is not a claim that every package has artifact provenance; NuGet Trusted Publishing authenticates publication and is not artifact provenance. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Documented pre-public/post-hardening audit fixes shipped promptly; the 2026-10-02 public inventory found no medium/high/critical-labeled unresolved reports and no advisory records. Review released fixes and any additional reports before submission; a 90-day disclosure policy is not itself proof of this 60-day criterion. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: All critical/high findings from pre-public and post-hardening audits were fixed before public release; see docs/security-audits/. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The 2026-10-02 repository secret-scanning API returned zero open alerts, with scanning and push protection enabled. This is a point-in-time repository observation, not proof of absence or a claim that runtime redaction covers every secret format. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
static_analysis_justification: Actual [CodeQL C#/JavaScript analyses](https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/actions/runs/36962352592) completed and uploaded results. The fresh-main scan reported six findings; their traces, confirmed temporary-file fix, and false-positive evidence are recorded in [the follow-up](security-quality-follow-up.md#merged-main-findings-and-disposition). Roslyn/format checks and Scorecard are separate controls. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: The exercised hosted CodeQL security-extended suite reported 63 C# and 103 JavaScript/TypeScript rules. The working rollout selects security-and-quality and adds Python; hosted execution and diagnostic triage remain required before claiming the expanded suite's coverage. Rule counts do not establish complete security coverage. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Confirmed unsafe temporary fixture writes were reproduced and repaired with an atomically created private directory; SQL findings were traced to benign test paths and actual provider encryption was checked. Fresh-main scan confirmation remains the closure gate. Historical audit fixes and accepted residual risks remain documented; future confirmed medium/higher exploitable findings still require timely fixes. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on main pushes, PRs and weekly; Roslyn/format checks run in CI. A new workflow does not retroactively scan historical commits. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
dynamic_analysis_justification: Actual [hosted SharpFuzz/libFuzzer run](https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/actions/runs/36960543729) instrumented ScriptDom/Guard, detected the separate deliberate engine crash, then completed 370,328 real inputs in 61 seconds with feature/corpus growth and no emitted product findings. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Shipping project code is C#/JavaScript, not a memory-unsafe language. The nonshipping upstream C++ fuzz bridge does not establish sanitizer coverage of all native dependencies. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz target has unconditional malformed/empty-acceptance, non-SELECT, SELECT-INTO and NEXT VALUE FOR invariants that throw even in Release builds. The actual post-repair campaign ran 36,985 inputs in 11 seconds and separately proved managed crash detection. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The confirmed temporary-file symlink overwrite was reproduced before and prevented after the fix. Parser/Guard fuzz campaigns emitted no product findings; the separate intentional engine-crash probe is not a vulnerability. Future confirmed findings still require timely fixes. Evidence: https://github.com/codegiveness/mssql-mcp/blob/main/docs/security-quality-follow-up.md
